description:
Need an application to manage fixed assets for organisation, It should be able to calculate depreciation as per Indian laws 
Should have the following requirement 
Asset Location : Identify where your assets are located by your branches , location within your branch and departments and option to assign to employees if required 

Asset Register : Asset register requirements as per Companies Act India including serial numbers, Make and model of the asset 
Depreciation calculation – Company’s Act (Monthly) and yearly 
Depreciation calculation – Income Tax (Annual) Process
Asset Installation: Feature to record and confirm the date of installation and other details 
Asset Transfer : Provision to record and transfer assets from one location to another
Asset Sales / Scrap : Provision to remove the asset from the Asset Register 
Asset confirmation : A process to undertake the physical confirmation of the assets 
Warranty and AMC tracking : Provision to track the validity of the warranty and an active AMC

=== CONFIRMED SCOPE AND COMPLEXITY (user-approved — this OVERRIDES any conflicting inference from the brief) ===
* Which functional areas should be included in the application?
  - Include: Asset Register; Locations & Assignment; Depreciation – Co. Act; Depreciation – Inc. Tax; Asset Lifecycle; Physical Verification; Warranty & AMC
  - EXCLUDE (explicitly declined by the user — do NOT specify these): Capital Budgeting
* How fully-featured should the initial build be?
  - Include: Standard
* Should any asset actions require a manager's approval before they are recorded?
  - Include: All key actions
* Which reports and outputs are essential for day-to-day use and audits?
  - Include: Depreciation Register; Verification Report; Warranty / AMC Expiry; Asset Register Report; Management Dashboard
Write the specification to cover EXACTLY this confirmed scope at the confirmed complexity level: include every confirmed item, honour every added point, and do not add functional areas, activities or enterprise features beyond it.
